en: O Agni, you [are born] from the heavens; you, O flame-seeker, [are born] from the waters and from the stone.

You [are born] from the forests and from the plants; you, O Lord of men, are born pure among men. Yours, O Agni, is the office of the Hotṛ; yours is the office of the Potṛ at the appointed time; yours is the office of the Neṣṭṛ; you are the Agnīdh for the one who follows the cosmic order (ṛta).
Thine is the office of the *praśāstṛ*; thou art the *adhvaryu*, and thou art the *brahmán* and the master of the house within our home.
O Agni, thou art Indra, the bull of the virtuous; thou art Viṣṇu, the wide-striding, worthy of adoration.
Thou art the *brahmán*, the winner of wealth, O *Brahmaṇaspati*; O Ordainer, thou art accompanied by *Puraṃdhi*.

O Agni, you are King Varuṇa, whose laws are firm; you become Mitra, O wonder-worker, worthy of praise. You are Aryaman, the lord of the good, from whom we share enjoyment; you are Aṃśa, O God, who distributes wealth at the assembly. O Agni, as Tvaṣṭṛ you bestow heroic vigor upon the worshiper; yours, O you of Mitra-like glory, is kinship with the divine wives.
You, O swift impeller, bestow abundance of good horses; you are the host of men, rich in many treasures.
O Agni, you are Rudra, the Asura of the great heaven; you are the host of Maruts; you rule over nourishment.
You travel with the ruddy winds, bringing peace to the home; as Pūṣan, you yourself protect those who worship you.
O Agni, you are the giver of wealth to him who prepares the offering; O God, you are Savitṛ, the bestower of treasures.
You are Bhaga, O Lord of men, and you rule over riches; you are the protector in the home for him who has served you.
O Agni, the people in their homes strive toward you as their lord of the clan, toward you, the benevolent king.
O you of beautiful countenance, you rule over all things; you are equal to ten hundred thousand.
O Agni, men seek you as a father with their sacrifices; they seek you, who shine with your own body, for brotherhood through their ritual labor.
You become a son to him who serves you; you are a most gracious friend; protect us from the assailant.

O Agni, you are the *Ṛbhu* at the break of dawn, worthy of homage; you are the lord of strength and of wealth consisting of food. Shining forth, you bestow [gifts] for the sake of giving; you are the one who instructs and extends the sacrifice.
O divine Agni, you are Aditi to the donor; as Hotrā Bhāratī, you grow strong through our song.
You are *Iḷā*, the giver of a hundred winters for skill; you, O Lord of Wealth, are *Sarasvatī*, the slayer of Vṛtra.
O Agni, well-maintained, you possess the highest vital power; in your desirable color, in your sight, are the glories.
You are the mighty strength that carries us across; you are abundant wealth, wide on every side.

O Agni, the Ādityas have made you their mouth; the pure ones have made you their tongue, O sole singer. Those who bestow gifts attend upon you at the sacrifices; through you the gods eat the offered oblation.
In you, O Agni, all the guileless ones, the gods, eat the offered oblation with their mouths.
Through you, mortals sweeten their libation; you, the pure one, were born as the embryo of the plants.

O Agni, well-born one, you are equal to them and even greater than they in your might; indeed, you surpass the gods. For when your greatness spreads abroad here, both heaven and earth, the two worlds, yield to it.

O Agni, those wise patrons who bestow upon the singers a bounty preeminent in cattle, horses, and ornaments—lead both us and them toward greater prosperity. May we, blessed with heroic sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
Increase Jātavedas through sacrifice; worship Agni with oblation and with a continuous song.
To him who is kindled, well-nourished, golden-hued, celestial, the Hotṛ-priest seated at the pole within the sacrificial assemblies—

to you, O Agni, the nights and dawns have lowed, as milch-cows low for their calf in the stalls. Like the radiance of heaven, O possessor of many boons, you shine forth through the human generations, binding together the nights.

The gods have established him, the doer of wondrous deeds, at the foundation of the mid-air as the messenger between heaven and earth— Agni, who is like a chariot to be recognized, possessing bright radiance, a friend to be praised among the people.
While he sprinkles himself in the mid-air within his own home, they have placed him, shining like the moon, within the enclosure.
The winged one of Pṛśni, observing with his eyes, like a guardian over the path, he extends across both races.
He is the Hotṛ; encompassing the entire sacrifice, men strive toward him with oblations and song.
With golden jaws, flickering among the growing plants, like the sky, he makes the two worlds manifest with his rays.
Enkindled for our well-being, O wealthy one, grant us prosperity; as one who bestows gifts, shine upon us with riches.
O Agni, bring the two worlds (*rodasī*) to us for our welfare, so that men may enjoy the oblations, O God.
O Agni, give us great wealth, give us thousandfold; like doors, open up strength for us through renown.

Make heaven and earth turn toward us with sacred prayer; make the bright dawns shine like the light of the sun. Enkindled in accordance with the radiant dawns and nights, he has shone forth with his ruddy luster.
Agni, the priest who makes the sacrifice perfect for man, is the king of the people and the gracious guest of the one who offers wealth.
Thus, O Agni, our ancient human prayers have swelled among the immortals in the high heavens.
Like a milch-cow, she yields for the singer in the sacrificial assemblies by her own power, providing food in hundreds of forms.
O Agni, may we surpass these people through our horses, or through our heroic strength, or through our sacred prayer.

May our splendor shine high above the five peoples, blazing aloft, invincible like the sun. Be mindful of us, O powerful one, worthy of praise, you in whom the well-born patrons find their strength. O Agni, that sacrifice which the prize-winners approach, shining brightly in your own home for the sake of perpetual offspring—[be mindful of us].
O Jātavedas, may we both—your praisers, O Agni, and our wise patrons—be under your protection.
Grant us wealth, riches that are many-colored, abundant, rich in progeny, and blessed with noble offspring.
[Grant this] to those who [bestow gifts] upon the praisers...
Kindled on the earth, Agni has been established; facing all beings, he stands.
May Agni—the purifier, the wise god from of old, the worthy one—sacrifice to the gods as the Hotṛ-priest.
Narāśaṃsa, anointing the stations, with his greatness reaches toward the three heavens, possessing celestial light.
Sprinkling the oblation with a mind dripping with clarity, may he anoint the gods at the head of the sacrifice.
O Agni, being praised by our mind as the one worthy of honor, sacrifice to the gods today before the human priest.
Bring hither the unshakable host of the Maruts; O men, worship Indra who sits upon the sacred grass.
O divine *barhis*, increasing, rich in heroes, spread upon the altar for the sake of wealth and easy to maintain—sit upon this, O Vasus, anointed with ghee, all you gods, Ādityas worthy of sacrifice!
May the divine doors, being invoked, open wide; they are easy of access through our salutations.
Spacious and undecaying, may they spread wide, purifying our glorious and heroic luster.
May Dawn and Night, the two who have grown great from of old, accomplish our noble works, like two joyous weavers.
Woven together, they weave the extended thread; they are the well-milking, milk-laden ornaments of the sacrifice.
The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first, most wise, shall sacrifice uprightly with their two radiant forms;
sacrificing to the gods in due season, they shall anoint them at the navel of the earth upon the three ridges.
Sarasvatī, who perfects our devotion, the goddess Iḷā, and Bhāratī, who overcomes all—[may they prosper us].
May the three goddesses, sitting upon this sacrificial grass (*barhis*) by their own inherent power, protect this flawless refuge.
A hero of golden hue, well-supported, bestowing vital strength, and loving the gods, is born through obedience.
May Tvaṣṭṛ open up offspring for us as our kinship; then may he go to the domain of the gods.
May the Lord of the Forest, releasing [the victim], stand near; may Agni prepare the oblation with his insights.
May the divine immolator, knowing well, lead the thrice-anointed offering to the gods. Ghee has been mixed; ghee is his birthplace; he rests in ghee; ghee is his domain.
According to your wont, bring [the gods] here; O Bull, rejoice and carry away the oblation consecrated with *svāhā*.

I invoke for you Agni, the one of brilliant luster, worthy of perfect praise, the guest of the people, and rich in offerings— He who, like Mitra, is to be cherished, the god among the divine folk, Jātavedas.
Worshipping him in the gathering place of the waters, the Bhr̥gus established him twice among the people of Āyu.
May this Agni, the messenger of the gods who possesses swift horses, surpass all beings.
The gods placed Agni, the beloved friend, among the human tribes as he dwelt there.
May he shine upon the longing nights, he who is to be honored in the house of the giver.
His prosperity is delightful like one's own; his appearance is lovely when he hastens, eager to act.
He who repeatedly stirs among the plants makes his tongue flicker like a chariot-horse tossing its tail.
When he comes, the forest-devourers praise my greatness; he has fashioned his color for those who offer oblations.
He is distinguished by his wondrous, gleaming light; though aged, he has suddenly become young again. He shines upon the forests like one parched with thirst, roaring like a chariot on its path.
The one whose path is black, the glowing and delightful one, has become manifest, smiling like the sky with its clouds.

He who has spread himself over the broad earth, he moves like a beast, self-reliant and without a herdsman; Agni, radiant with flame, burning down the forests, his path blackened, has made the earth savory.
Now, for the sake of remembering your former favor, this prayer has been recited at the third assembly.
O Agni, grant us great wealth consisting of many heroes, abundant food, and riches accompanied by noble offspring.
Just as through you, O Agni, the Gṛtsamadas have overcome their enemies and won them over in secret.

Possessing brave heroes, overcoming those who attack us—grant that vital strength to our patrons and to the singer. The perceptive Hotṛ has been born, the father for the protection of his fathers; may we be able to direct that noble wealth which is to be won by the prize-seekers.

In whom the seven reins are extended, the leader of the sacrifice—the eighth one is divine, like Manu; as the *potṛ* priest, he promotes all that. Or rather, when he has run along after these [reins] and has uttered the sacred prayers (*brahmāṇi*), then he indeed impels them.
He has encompassed all poetic wisdoms as the felly encompasses the wheel.
For he was born together with pure mental power, a pure director of rites;
knowing his firm laws, he grows like branches.
These milch-cows, seeking their own color, have followed him, the Neṣṭṛ-priest;
are they not better than the three sisters who have gone there? When the sister has come near her mother, she stands bearing the clarified butter.
The Adhvaryu rejoices at their arrival, as grain does at the rain.
Let the priest perform his priestly office for his own sustenance.
May we win the praise-song and the sacrifice with reverence; we have offered them.
RV 2.5.8.1: Just as the wise man shall prepare [the sacrifice] for all the worshipful ones, so may this sacrifice which we have performed be centered in you, O Agni.
RV 2.6.1.1: O Agni, accept this my fuel-stick and this my attendance. RV 2.6.1.2: And truly, hear these songs of mine.
With this [hymn], O Agni, son of strength, we worship thee who art fond of horses;
with this well-spoken hymn, O thou of noble birth.
Thee, who art fond of songs, the seeker of wealth, the giver of wealth—we worship with our songs.
May we, as those who offer worship, pay you honor. Be mindful of us, O liberal patron, lord of wealth, giver of riches;
drive away from us all those who hate us.
May he [grant] us rain from heaven; may he [grant] us unassailable booty;
may he [grant] us nourishments by the thousands.
O youngest messenger, for us who praise you and seek your help, [come] through our song.
O most excellent sacrificer, O Hotṛ, come hither! O Agni, O sage, you move between both races of men as one who knows them;
you are the envoy for both the human and the friendly (divine) folk.
As one who knows, you have pleased us; O wise one, sacrifice in due order.
Sit down upon this sacred grass (barhis).
O youngest Agni, descendant of Bharata, bring hither the most excellent and radiant wealth.
O Vasu, [grant us] wealth desired by many. Let not the hostility of either god or mortal prevail over us; deliver us from that enmity.
And through you, may we cross over all enemies, as one crosses over the flowing streams of water.
O Agni, pure, purifying, and worthy of praise, you shine forth mightily.
You, O Agni, are invoked with offerings of clarified butter;
you, O Bhārata Agni, are invoked by us with offerings of barren cows, bulls,
and eight-footed mares.
Feeding on wood, with clarified butter as his libation, the ancient, excellent Hotṛ-priest,
the wonderful son of strength—
praise now the yoking of Agni’s chariots as one who seeks for booty.
Of the most glorious and bountiful one;
he who is a good leader for the donor, who, being ageless himself, causes the enemy to age, and whose countenance is beautiful when invoked.
He who is praised for his splendor in the homes at evening and at dawn,
whose sacred law (*vrata*) is never violated;
he who shines forth, variegated with light, like the sun with his radiance.
Anointed with unaging [fats], they have strengthened Agni with hymns according to his own sovereignty;
he has assumed all splendors.
Through the protections of Agni, Indra, Soma, and the gods, may we remain unharmed; may we overcome those who attack us.
The Hotṛ, knowing his place, has sat down upon the seat of the Hotṛ—blazing, resplendent, and most skillful.
Agni, whose vigilance over his vows is unassailable, is the most excellent; he is the bringer of thousands, pure-tongued.
You are our messenger, you are our protector from afar; O Bull, you are the leader to greater wealth.
O Agni, shining brightly, be the watchful guardian of our offspring and of our bodies, never failing us.
Let us worship you in your highest birthplace, O Agni; let us worship with hymns in your lower dwelling place.
From whatever womb you have arisen, I sacrifice to that; into you, when well-kindled, they have poured the oblations.
O Agni, as the most excellent sacrificer, perform the sacrifice with the oblation; with readiness, acknowledge the gift and the wealth bestowed.
For you indeed are the lord of riches; you are the inspirer of the pure word.
Your twofold wealth, O wonder-worker, does not diminish day after day as you are born.
Make the singer, O Agni, possessed of food; make him the master of wealth consisting of noble offspring.
With his army, he is well-disposed toward us; the best of sacrificers, he worships the gods for our well-being.
O Agni, being undeceived, a guardian, and a protector from afar, shine upon us with splendor and wealth.
Agni is to be invoked first like a father, when he has been kindled by man at the place of the oblation.
Clothed in glory, immortal, discerning, worthy of being groomed, and seeking renown is that prize-winning steed.
May Agni, of wondrous luster, the immortal and discerning one, hear my call with all my songs.
Two dark steeds, or two red ones, or two ruddy ones draw his chariot; he, the distributor, has fashioned it.
Upon her who lies supine, they brought forth the well-born one; Agni became the embryo within those of many forms.
Even in the dark night, the wise one dwells unconfined by his great splendors. I sprinkle Agni with the oblation of ghee, him who abides facing all the worlds.
Broad, vast with transverse vigor, most expansive, impetuous, and visible through his food—him, who faces every direction, I besprinkle; may he accept that with a mind free from demons.
Agni, possessing the beauty of a youth and a desirable hue, flickering with his body, cannot be touched.
O Victorious One, may you by choice accept your portion; with you as our messenger, let us speak like Manu.
With my eloquent tongue, I invoke the perfect Agni, who is rich in sweetness and a winner of wealth.
Hear our call, O Indra; do not neglect it. May we be yours for the giving of riches.
For these strengthening draughts, seeking wealth, increase you as rivers flow.
Release the great waters, O Indra, which you caused to swell—the many that were obstructed by the serpent, O Hero.
Strengthened by hymns of praise, you shattered even the Dāsa who considered himself immortal.
O Hero Indra, we now delight in these hymns of praise and in these Rudra-like songs of praise;
for you, in them, rejoicing, these [soma-drops] flow forth like bright [steeds] toward Vāyu. Increasing your brilliant strength and placing the brilliant thunderbolt in your arms—
O Indra, growing strong for us, may you, the radiant one, overcome the Dāsa tribes with the help of Sūrya.
You slew the serpent who lay hidden in secret, concealed and dwelling within the waters— him, the master of magic arts,
who had obstructed the waters and stayed the heavens, O Hero, by your heroic power.

We shall now praise your ancient greatness, O Indra, and we shall praise your recent deeds. We shall praise the thunderbolt yearning in your arms; we shall praise your two bay steeds, the banners of the Sun.
Let your two bay steeds, O Indra, seeking booty, let loose their neighing that drips with clarity.
The earth spread itself out on every side; even the mountain that was about to flee took firm stand. The mountain sat down, never wavering; bellowing toward his mothers, he has stepped forth.
Strengthening their voice at the farthest limit, they have spread abroad the pipe impelled by Indra.
Indra struck down Vṛtra, the wielder of magic, who lay across the great river.
Out of fear, the two worlds, heaven and earth, trembled at the roar of this bull and his thunderbolt. The thunderbolt of this bull roared aloud when he, a mortal, utterly consumed the non-human foe.
He struck down the magical powers of the guileful Dānava after drinking of the pressed juice. O heroic Indra, drink, drink the Soma; let the exhilarating pressed juices delight you.
Filling your two flanks, let them cause you to swell; thus the pressed juice has helped Indra in the battle for the city.
In thee, O Indra, we have found refuge; as inspired singers, may we win wisdom, serving according to the Eternal Law (ṛta).
Seeking thy help, we meditate upon thy praise; may we be present at once for the granting of thy wealth.
May we be thine, O Indra, those who through thy protection seek thy aid, increasing our strength.

O Gods, grant us that most powerful wealth which we desire—wealth accompanied by heroic sons. Grant us a dwelling; grant us a friend; O Indra, grant us the host of Maruts. And may those who are of one mind and rejoicing, the Vāyus, drink the first portion of the offering.

May they now come, in whom you take delight; drink the Soma to your satisfaction, O Indra, and be strong! As a deliverer, you have well protected us in battles and have exalted the heavens with great hymns of praise.
Indeed, those who are great and who seek to win your favor through their songs of praise—O Deliverer!—[may they come].
Spreading the sacred grass like a dwelling, they have come, O Indra, protected by thee, to win the prize.
O Hero, rejoicing now among the fierce ones, drink the Soma at the Trikadruka sacrifices, O Indra.
Shaking your beard, being gratified, come with your two bay horses to drink of the pressed juice.
O Hero, assume that power wherewith you struck down Vṛtra, the Dānu, and Aurṇavābha. You disclosed the light for the Ārya; the Dasyu was cast down on your left, O Indra.
May we, who overcome all rivalries with your aids, conquer the Dasyus through the Ārya.
For us, you delivered that Viśvarūpa, the son of Tvaṣṭṛ, to Trita, the friend of the Sākhi.
Increasing in strength, you struck down Arbuda with this exhilarating pressed juice of Trita.
Like the sun rolling back its wheel, Indra, accompanied by the Aṅgirases, split Vala apart.

RV_02.011.21.1 Now may that wealthy sacrificial fee of yours, O Indra, yield a boon to the singer. RV_02.011.21.2 Bestow gifts upon those who praise you; let not our fortune fail us. May we speak aloud at the assembly. RV_02.012.01.1 He who, as soon as born, was the first wise god, who by his power encompassed the gods.
At whose very breath the two worlds trembled through the greatness of his manly power— he, O people, is Indra.
He who steadied the quaking earth, he who calmed the agitated mountains,
he who measured out the wide mid-air, he who propped up the heavens— he, O people, is Indra.

He who, having slain the serpent, set free the seven rivers; he who drove out the cows by stripping away the obstruction of Vala; he who generated fire between the two stones, the devourer in battles—he is Indra.
By him all these moving things were made to tremble; he who cast down the Dāsa race into the depths.
