He who is the impeller of the weary, he who is the helper of the emaciated, he who is the protector of the suppliant Brahmin and the poor man;

he who, fair-cheeked, is the guardian of him who has set the pressing-stones in motion and pressed the Soma—may he grant us prosperity. In whose direction are the horses, in whose direction are the cattle, in whose direction are the villages, and in whose direction are all chariots.
He who generated the sun and the dawn, he who is the leader of the waters—he is Indra.
To whom the two armies, meeting in conflict, cry out for help; whom both enemies, the higher and the lower, invoke—he is Indra.
Though they have mounted the same chariot, those who call upon him separately—he is Indra.
Without whom people do not conquer, whom those engaged in battle invoke for protection;
he who has become the counterpart of all, he who shakes the unshakable—O Lord of the *sajīvan* (the living host).
He who with his arrow struck down the many who committed great sin and who did not acknowledge [his power].
He who does not yield to the arrogance of the defiant one, he who is the slayer of the Dasyu.
He who discovered Śambara dwelling among the mountains in the fortieth autumn;
he who slew the serpent Ahi as he was displaying his might, the son of Danu as he lay there.
He who, the bull with seven rays, the mighty one, let loose the seven rivers to flow;
he who, thunderbolt-armed, struck down Rauhiṇa as he was scaling heaven. Even Heaven and Earth bow down before him; even the mountains tremble at his might.
RV_02.012.13.2 He who is the drinker of Soma, who is gathered [in power], whose arms hold the thunderbolt, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand—he is the one to be praised.

RV_02.012.14.1 He who protects with his aid the one who presses the juice, the one who cooks, the one who recites, and the one who exerts himself; RV_02.012.14.2 He for whom prayer is a means of increase, for whom is the Soma, and for whom is this gift—he is the one to be praised.
You who, even for the one who presses the juice and cooks the oblation, break open the stubborn [enemy] for booty—you are indeed truly real.
O Indra, may we, being always dear to you and possessing brave sons, proclaim our wisdom at the assembly.
The Season is the progenitor; having been born quickly from its waters, he entered into them, wherein he grows.
Then she became overflowing with milk; that first cream of the stalk was worthy of praise.
They come together, carrying milk; they bring forth nourishment for the one who possesses all abundance.
The path is common, following the downward slopes, which you made for the one who follows the law; this is your first deed, worthy of praise.
One speaks after [the other] regarding what he gives; one goes about changing those forms, [measuring] those waters.
One endures all the thrusts of the other, who has performed those [deeds].
They sit distributing nourishment to their offspring; like wealth, they attend to the back that rises up for the one who approaches.
Unwearied, with his tusks he eats the food of his father—he who made...
You made the earth visible to heaven; you, the slayer of Ahi, cleared the paths for the rivers.
The gods have generated you, a god, with hymns of praise like water for a prize-winning steed; you are worthy of our lauds.
You who bestow both food and nourishment, you have milked from the moist the dry and the honeyed;
you have laid down a treasure for Vivasvat, for you alone rule over all.
You who, by your law, have established in the gift the flowering plants and the fruit-bearing trees, and the flowing waters.
And he who begat the peerless lightnings of heaven—[O] Wide One, [bring them] wide around us.
He who brought Nārmara, together with his wealth, for the sake of slaying, for nourishment, and for the dwelling of Dāsa;
By means of the strengthening [weapon], the unassailable mouth—and thus today, O doer of much, [be] our protector.
He at whose command a hundred or ten were eaten together, when you, being urged, protected him in his obedience;

for Dabhīti, you bound the Dasyus without cords and became one who is most helpful to the well-protected. All the fortresses yielded to his manly power; they bestowed wealth upon him, the achiever of deeds.
You have propped up the six expanses, the five visible realms; you have become the one who encompasses them all.
O Hero, your heroic power is well-proclaimed, since by a single resolve you win wealth.
O Indra, worthy of praise for all these deeds, you have performed all the exploits of Jātūṣṭhira, the powerful one—[those] vital strengths which you achieved.
You brought to rest the swift-flowing waters for easy crossing; you made a path for Turvīti and Vayya.
You raised up the outcast who was lying low, bestowing glory upon the blind and the lame.
O Vasu, prepare that bounty for us to give; great indeed is your wealth.
O Indra, whatever is wondrous for the sake of glory throughout the days—may we speak it aloud, O Vasus and Sādhyas.
O Adhvaryus, bring the Soma for Indra; pour out the exhilarating juice with the *āmitra* vessels.
For the Hero desires his drink evermore; offer it to the Bull, for he truly longs for this.
O Adhvaryus, bring this [Soma] for him who struck down Vṛtra—who had enclosed the waters—just as a thunderbolt strikes a tree;
Indra, being desirous of it, deserves the drinking of this.
O Adhvaryus, he who struck down Dṛbhīka, who drove out the cows, and who indeed opened Vala for you.
For him, clothe Indra with Soma-offerings in the mid-air,
as one clothes a swift steed with garments. O Adhvaryus, him who slew the ram that had displayed its nine-and-ninety arms—
him who cast Arbuda down and crushed him— drive that Indra to the offering of Soma.
O Adhvaryus, offer the soma-juice to that Indra who slew Svashna, who slew the insatiable Shushna, who [slew] Vyasas;
who [slew] Pipru, Namuchi, and Rudhikra—to that Indra, offer the draught.
O Adhvaryus, he who shattered the hundred fortresses of Shambara, as many as they were, like stones—[to him, offer the draught].
Indra, who scattered the hundred and the thousand of Varcin—bring Soma for him!
O Adhvaryus, bring Soma for him who, having slain [the foe], cast down a hundred and a thousand into the lap of the earth;
he who struck down the heroes of Kutsa, Ayu, and Atithigva. Bring Soma for him!
O Adhvaryus, whatever you men desire, bring that to Indra with obedience; carrying it, may you attain it. O ye who sacrifice, bring the Soma purified by the hands for the famous Indra and offer it.
O Adhvaryus, perform service for him; pour forth what has been purified in the wooden vat into the wooden vessel.
Rejoicing, he has lowed toward the offering in your hand; O Adhvaryus, pour out the intoxicating Soma for Indra.
O Adhvaryus, mix it with the milk of the cow; satisfy the liberal Indra with the Soma juices.
I know this secret of his; the worshipful one perceives me as desiring to give even more.

O Adhvaryus, he who is the king of celestial wealth, of the earth, and of that which dwells upon it—fill him, Indra, with Soma as one fills a granary with barley; let this be your work for us. To us, let that...
Now, indeed, I shall proclaim the great, true deeds of this great and true one. At the Trikadruka rites, he drank of this pressed juice; in its exhilaration, Indra slew the dragon.
He propped up the vast sky where there was no pillar; he filled the two worlds and the mid-air.
He supported the earth and spread it out; Indra performed these deeds in the exhilaration of Soma.
Like a dwelling, he measured out the eastward-flowing channels with his measures; with his thunderbolt, he pierced the channels of the rivers.
He released them at will along paths for long journeys; Indra performed these deeds in the exhilaration of Soma.
Having surrounded his attackers from all sides, he placed all their weapons into the kindled fire;
he bestowed upon him cattle, horses, and chariots.
He stilled that great roaring river and brought those who had not bathed safely across to the other shore.
Having emerged from the waters, they stood forth toward wealth; he, with his greatness, sent the upward-flowing river Sindhu. With his thunderbolt, he crushed the Dawns;
rending those who were powerless, he struck them down with his swift weapons.
That wise one, appearing as the hidden lover of maidens, rose up from afar;
the cripple stood firm and he looked out across the forest.
Praised by the Aṅgirases, he split Vala and shattered the firm foundations of the mountain.
He broke down their artificial embankments...
By means of sleep, you overpowered Cumuri and Dhuni; you slew the Dasyu and protected Dabhīti.
Even the pillar found gold there...
RV_02.015.10.1 Surely she will respond to you... RV_02.016.01.1 To him who is the most excellent among the good, I offer a fair hymn of praise, like an oblation into a kindled fire.
RV_02.016.01.2 We invoke for our protection Indra, the undecaying one who causes others to age, the grown one, eternally young.
Without whom, the great Indra, nothing exists; in him all heroic powers are gathered together.

He carries Soma in his belly, vast strength in his body, the thunderbolt in his hand, and wisdom in his head. Your power, O Indra, cannot be encompassed by the two worlds, nor can your chariot be contained by the oceans or the mountains.
No one can reach your thunderbolt when you fly across many leagues with your swift steeds.
For all bring forth their will for him, the worshipful, the bold, the bull who grants his favor.
As a bull, sacrifice with the oblation, O most wise one; drink the Soma, Indra, with your bull-like luster.
The vessel of the bull flows forth, a wave of honey, for the bull to drink—the bull who provides bull-like food.
The two Adhvaryu priests are bulls, the pressing-stones are bulls; they press the bull Soma for the Bull.
Thy thunderbolt is a bull, and thy chariot is a bull; thy two bay steeds are bulls, and thy weapons are bull-like.

O Bull, you rule over the exhilarating draught; O Indra, drink your fill of the bull-like Soma. Like one skilled in speech, I approach you with a prayer at the libations, bold as I am in the assembly, as if approaching a ship.
Will he not surely take heed of this our word? We pour out Indra like a fountain of wealth.
Turn toward us before the distress comes, as a cow, swelling with milk, turns to her calf in the pasture.
O Śatakratu, may we once more be united with your favors, as husbands are joined with their wives.
Now indeed that...

Sing this new song for him, as did the Aṅgirases, when his vital powers surge forth as of old; when, in the exhilaration of Soma, he with his might threw open all the cow-pens that were encompassed and fortified. May he be present, he who, measuring out strength for the first nourishment, surpassed even greatness itself.
The hero who, in battles, clothed his body and by his greatness fastened the sky upon his head.
You performed your first great heroic deed when, at the beginning, you stirred up your fury with sacred prayer (*brahman*).
Shaken off by the one who stands on the chariot drawn by tawny steeds, the swift ones rush forth together and apart.
Then he, who by his might surpassed all worlds, grew strong as the lord of power;
the bearer [of light] spread out heaven and earth with radiance, weaving together and dispelling the thick darkness.
He, by his vigorous strength, made firm the mountains facing the east and turned the waters downward.
He supported the earth that nourishes all, and by his creative power (*māyā*) he propped up the sky so it would not fall.
That [strength] was sufficient for his two arms, which his father fashioned from every kind of knowledge and existence.
With that thunderbolt, the one of mighty roar struck down Krivi upon the earth, so that he might lie there.
Like a maiden who has not yet reached maturity, dwelling with her parents, I have come to you from a common seat; I have sought Bhaga.
Make a sign for me, bestow it upon me, and grant me that portion for my body which you will give to me.
O Indra, we invoke you as a liberal giver; you, O Indra, are the one who bestows works and spoils of war.
Help us, O Indra, with your wondrous aid; being a destroyer, O Indra, make us more prosperous.
Now indeed that...
At dawn the new chariot has been harnessed—the prize-winning one, with four yokes, three whips, and seven reins.
The man with ten fingers, winner of light, has become swift through his sacrifices and prayers.
He is ready for him the first time, he the second, and even the third—man’s Hotar-priest. One bears the germ of another; others have brought him forth. He, the noble bull, unites himself with others.
Now, with a new and well-spoken word, let us yoke the two bay steeds to Indra’s chariot.
Let not the many other wise sacrificers detain you here.
O Indra, come hither drawn by two bay steeds; come with four, come with six, being invoked.
With eight or ten [steeds], come to this pressed Soma for the drinking; O liberal one, do not neglect us.

Come hither with twenty, with thirty, or with forty bay horses, you who are worthy of sacrifice. O Indra, come with fifty well-yoked chariots, or with sixty, or with seventy, to the drinking of the Soma.
Come hither with eighty, with ninety, or being carried by a hundred bay horses;
for this Soma among the Śunahotras has been poured out for you, O Indra, through devotion to you, for your exhilaration.
Come toward my prayer, O Indra; place all two bay steeds at the pole of your chariot.
For you have become one to be invoked in many places; O Hero, rejoice at this libation!
May my friendship with Indra never be severed; may his sacrificial fee yield for us.
Under his most excellent protection and in his hand, may we be victors in every endeavor.
Surely she...
[for the exhilaration] of this drinkable stalk, for the wise one, of the pressed nourishment;
that in which Indra, increasing from of old, has established his dwelling, as have the men who cherish the sacred word.
Intoxicated by this mead, Indra, thunderbolt in hand, rent asunder the dragon that encompassed the floods.
When his vital strength rushed toward the pastures and the refreshments of the rivers,
the mighty Indra, slayer of the dragon, drove the waters toward the ocean.
He generated the sun, he found the cattle; with night he established the ordinances of the days.
He, Indra, bestows many invincible boons upon the man who offers gifts; he slays Vṛtra.
He who has become instantly accessible to men contending for the acquisition of the sun.
Indra, the god, being praised, released the sun for the sake of the mortal who presses the soma;
when Etaśa, bestowing a portion, brought him wealth that was hidden and free from reproach.
He delivered the insatiable Śuṣṇa and Kuyava to Kutsa, who had the heavenly charioteer as his ally.
For Divodāsa, Indra shattered ninety-nine fortresses of Śambara.

Thus, O Indra, we have fashioned this hymn for you, seeking glory as if by our own selves, striving for strength. May we, aspiring for it, attain that seventh [step]—may the weapon of the god who hates us not strike us down.
Thus the Gṛtsamadas, O Hero, have fashioned for thee new hymns, seeking thy favor; desiring sacred prayer, O Indra, may they attain food, strength, a secure dwelling, and bliss.
Now indeed that...
O Indra, we are yours; take note of us well! We bring forth our offerings like those seeking booty for their chariot.
Singing praises and reflecting with inspired thought, we desire the favor of a hero such as you.
O Indra, through your protections, you guard the people who are devoted to you and seek your assistance.
O Indra, you are the protector of the one who offers oblations; thus, may he who approaches you with devotion be yours.

O youthful Indra, may that friend of ours be one to be invoked repeatedly—may he be our auspicious guardian and the protector of men, who by his aid shall lead forward the one who recites, the one who exerts himself, the one who cooks the offering, and the one who praises.
I praise that Indra, I laud him, in whom men of old grew strong and found their rest. May he, being entreated, fulfill the desire for wealth of the modern man who offers prayer.
He, Indra, having delighted in the hymns of the Aṅgirases, strengthened them; seeking a path, he furthered their prayer.
Stealing away the splendor of the dawns while being praised by Sūrya, he shattered even the ancient strongholds of Aśna.
He is indeed the god renowned by the name Indra; standing upright for the sake of man, he is the most wondrous of all.
Overpowering the beloved [offspring] of the stingy Aśasāna, that self-dependent one struck off the head of the Dāsa.

That Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra and destroyer of forts, drove away the Dāsa women of dark origin. He generated for mankind both the earth and the waters; he ever strengthened the praise of the sacrificer.
To him, the powerful Indra, all was granted by the gods in the struggle for the waters.
When he brought his thunderbolt down upon his arms, having slain the Dasyus, he shattered their iron fortresses.
Now indeed that...
To him who conquers all, who conquers wealth, who conquers heaven, who conquers by force, who conquers men, and who conquers fertile fields.
Winning horses, winning cattle, winning the waters—bring the beloved Soma to Indra, the one worthy of sacrifice.

To the overcomer, the shatterer, the victor, the unconquered, the subduer, the ordainer; To the one of mighty stride, the bearer, the one who cannot be overcome, the all-conquering—to Indra, speak your homage.
The ever-conquering one, the devourer of men, the subduer of people, the shaker, the warrior, grown strong according to his will;
the gatherer of hosts, the victorious one, poured forth among the tribes—I shall proclaim the heroic deeds performed by Indra.
The unyielding bull, the slayer of the defiant, the deep, the lofty, whose wisdom is unattainable.
The impeller of the weak, the piercer, the firm, the broad—Indra, the performer of good sacrifices, generated the dawn and the sun.
By means of sacrifice, the wise and longing seekers found the path across the waters; they sent forth their prayers and attained their desires.
Seeking aid, through invocations and settled rites, they won the cattle; and by sending forth their thoughts toward Indra, they obtained riches.
O Indra, bestow upon us the most excellent riches, the insight of skill, and good fortune;
grant us the increase of wealth, the safety of our bodies, the sweetness of speech, and fair days.
At the Trikadruka sacrifices, the mighty and powerful buffalo drank his fill of the barley-mixed Soma pressed by Viṣṇu, according to his desire.
He has exhilarated him for the performance of great deeds; the great and wide one, the god, has accompanied the god, the true Indu [has accompanied] the true Indra.
Then, radiant with brilliance, he overcame Krivi by his might in battle; he filled the two worlds, heaven and earth, with his majesty and grew ever stronger.
He placed one [portion] within his belly, while the other overflowed; it [the soma] has accompanied him...
Born together with wisdom, you have grown great with might; increased together with heroic deeds, you are the subduer of enemies, O far-seeing one.

You are the giver of wealth and desirable riches to the one who praises you; he [the worshipper]—him... O dancer, Indra, that manly deed of yours, the first and ancient one performed in heaven, is to be proclaimed.
That by the god’s might he set the breath free and released the waters; he has become superior to all through his strength. May the Lord of a Hundred Powers find nourishment;
may he find food. We invoke you, the Lord of hosts, the sage among sages, possessed of the highest renown.
O Bṛhaspati, Lord of Prayer, you who are the eldest king of prayers, hearing us with your aids, sit upon your seat.
O Bṛhaspati, even the wise gods have attained your divine and worshipful portion.
Like the sun with its light awakens the dawn, you are the great progenitor of all sacred prayers through your power.

Having dispelled the waters and the darknesses, you mount the radiant chariot of *ṛta*, O Bṛhaspati—terrible, the subduer of enemies, the slayer of demons, the breaker of enclosures, and the finder of heaven.
By your wise guidances, you lead and protect the person who offers gifts to you; no distress shall reach him.

O Bṛhaspati, you are the scorcher of those who hate the *brahman* and the subduer of their wrath; great indeed is that majesty of yours. No distress, no misfortune from any quarter, no enemies, nor the double-tongued can overcome him whom you, O Brahmaṇaspati, protect as a good guardian; you drive away all deceivers from him.
You are our protector, the maker of paths, the far-seeing; for your service we age with our prayers.
O Bṛhaspati, whoever lays a snare for us, may his own calamity, full of fury, crush him. Or if some hostile mortal, seeking to harm us, should injure us though we are innocent—like a lurking wolf.
O Bṛhaspati, turn him away from our path; make this sacrifice of ours a smooth way for the feast of the gods.
We invoke you as the protector of our bodies, the savior, the advocate who is well-disposed toward us. O Bṛhaspati, strike down those who revile the gods; let not the evil-doers attain further favor.
Through you, O Bṛhaspati, who increase us well, may we bestow upon men desirable riches.
Those enemies who from afar or from near at hand assail us—crush them, so that they have no wealth.
Through you as our companion, O Bṛhaspati, who are full and bountiful, may we attain supreme vitality.

May the malevolent one who seeks to harm us not prevail; may we, through our well-spoken hymns, cross over to prosperity. The bull who does not yield, who goes to the challenge, is the scorcher of the enemy and the conqueror in battles.
O Brahmaṇaspati, you are the true one who exacts debts; you are the subduer even of the fierce, the tamer of the impetuous.

He who, with a godless mind, seeks to harm us, thinking himself fierce as he wishes to strike us down—O Bṛhaspati, let his deadly weapon not reach us; we ward off the wrath of that arrogant one who acts with evil intent.
To be invoked in battles, to be approached with homage, the one who goes forth to contests for booty and wins every prize.

Bṛhaspati has utterly crushed all those who seek to harm us and our enemies, like chariots. With your most piercing heat, burn the demons who have held you in contempt, O you of proven heroism. Make manifest that which is worthy of praise for you; O Bṛhaspati, destroy the adversaries.
O Bṛhaspati, that which surpasses the enemy, which shines brilliantly and powerfully among men,

and which, born of Truth, glows with might— that wonderful wealth bestow upon us. Do not deliver us to the thieves, those who dwell in the place of malice, the enemies who watch greedily for our food.
O Bṛhaspati, the gods do not deceive the heart; no one knows the Sāman better than you.

For Tvaṣṭṛ, the seer, brought you forth from all beings, from every Sāman. He is the avenger of debts, the debt-collector, the Lord of Prayer (Brahmaṇaspati), the slayer of the deceitful, the upholder of the great Cosmic Order (Ṛta).
For thy glory the mountain opened wide; when thou, O Aṅgiras, didst release the stall of the cows.
With Indra as thy ally, O Bṛhaspati, thou didst cast down the ocean that was encompassed by darkness.
O Brahmaṇaspati, be the director of this hymn; be mindful of it and prosper our offspring.

RV 2.23.19.2: All that which the gods protect is auspicious; may we speak forth the great [word]. RV 2.24.1.1: Favour this offering, you who are the lord; we shall worship you with this new and great song.
RV 2.24.1.2: So that our liberal patron may be praised as your friend, O Bṛhaspati, grant success to our prayer.
He who, bending those who were unbendable by his might, shattered the fortresses of Śambara with his fury;
Brahmaṇaspati caused even the immovable mountains to tremble and entered the mountain rich in treasures.
That deed, which was most divine among the gods, they performed: they loosened what was firm and made the solid things yield.
He drove forth the cows; with the sacred word (*brahman*) he split Vala asunder; he concealed the darkness and made the sun visible.
Brahmaṇaspati, by his might, pierced the well with its stone-mouthed opening, which had a stream of honey.
All those who behold the light drank from that very well; together they poured out the oceanic flood.
Ancient indeed are those worlds that have come to be; through the months and autumns, the doors have been opened for you.
Moving one toward the other without effort, Brahmaṇaspati has established the ordinances. Those who, approaching, have reached the treasure of the Paṇis, hidden away in the highest secret place—
Those wise ones, having recognized the falsehoods, returned; from where they had departed, they rose up again to enter.
The truth-abiding sages, having recognized the falsehoods, stood once more upon the great paths from whence they had come.
With their two arms, they kindled the fire upon the stone; there is no one who can escape it, for they have abandoned that which is alien.
With his swift bow whose string is the *ṛta*, Brahmaṇaspati reaches whatever he desires;
excellent are his arrows with which he shoots. Those who behold men and originate from the ear are for him to see.
He is the one who leads together, he who leads apart, the domestic priest; he is the well-praised Brahmaṇaspati in battle.

When the sighted one brings forth strength through his thought, he wins the wealth; then the sun shines and the two worlds glow with heat at will. The far-reaching and powerful [gifts] of Bṛhaspati, the most bountiful, are easy to find and worthy of attainment.
These are the gains of the beloved, vigorous one, by which both classes of people—the clans—enjoy themselves.
He who is all-pervading in the lower enclosure, the great and joyous one, has grown mighty through his own power;
that god has spread himself wide against the gods, for Brahmaṇaspati encompasses them all. All is true, O Maghavans; even the waters do not violate your sacred law.
O Indra and Brahmaṇaspati, come to our oblation and our food like two prize-winning horses yoked together.

And the most swift bearers hear [the call]; the eloquent one, fit for the assembly, brings forth prayers and wealth. With firm enmity, according to his will, he collects the debt; he indeed is the prize-winner, Brahmaṇaspati, in the encounter.
The true wrath of Brahmaṇaspati became manifest according to his will, as he was about to perform a mighty deed.
He who drove forth the cows distributed them across the sky; like a great stream, he flowed apart with his might.
O Brahmaṇaspati, may we ever be masters of well-governed wealth and of chariots filled with vital strength.
Bestow heroes upon our heroes; since you, as the Lord, come to my invocation through this sacred prayer (*brahman*).
O Brahmanaspati, you are the master of this... Kindling the fire, he shall conquer those who attack him; having performed the sacred prayer and offered the oblation, he shall prosper.
Born with him at his birth, he spreads forth along with him—whomever Brahmaṇaspati makes his ally.
With heroes he shall conquer the hero-slaying enemies; with cattle he shall extend his wealth and be mindful by himself.
His offspring and his progeny increase—whomever...
Like the surging flood of a river, he is impetuous; like a bull against castrated oxen, he prevails by his might over those who attack him.
Like the spreading flame of fire, he cannot be turned back—whomever [he aims at]. For him flow the celestial, unfailing waters; as the first among heroes, he goes forth in search of cattle.
He whose vital power is unassailable, who slays by his might—whomever...
To him all the roaring rivers flow; they have provided many flawless shelters.
Blessed with good fortune in the favor of the gods, he prospers—whomever...
The one whose prayer is upright shall conquer those who attack him; the seeker of the gods shall overcome the godless.
May he be a good protector and conquer in battles that are difficult to cross; let the sacrificer divide the food from the non-sacrificer.
Sacrifice, O hero; go forth against those who plot; direct your mind toward auspiciousness in the conquest of Vṛtra.
Prepare the oblation so that you may be fortunate; we choose for ourselves the protection of Brahmaṇaspati.

He indeed, with his people, with his clan, with his kin, and with his sons, wins booty and wealth through his men—he who, with a mind full of faith, honors with an oblation Brahmaṇaspati, the father of the gods.

He who has honored him with oblations rich in ghee—him Brahmaṇaspati leads forward. He delivers him from distress, guards him from harm; even from great misery, the wonderful one makes wide room for him. These songs, dripping with ghee, I ever offer with the ladle to the Ādityas, the kings.
May Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, the well-born Varuṇa, Dakṣa, and Aṃśa hear us. May Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, being of one mind, accept this hymn of praise from me today—
the Ādityas, who are pure, cleansed by the stream [of Soma], free from crookedness, blameless, and unharmed.
Those Ādityas are vast and profound, undeceived, many-eyed, and intent on detecting the deceiver;
they perceive both the crooked and the upright within, for even the most distant things are not hidden from these kings.
The Ādityas sustain all that moves and stands; they are the gods, the guardians of the entire world.

The far-sighted ones, guarding their divine power, observers of cosmic order (*ṛta*), exacting debts. O Ādityas, may I obtain this aid of yours, which, O Aryaman, brings comfort even in the midst of fear.
Under your guidance, O Mitra and Varuṇa, may I avoid misfortunes as one avoids pitfalls.
For easy to travel is your path, O Aryaman and Mitra; it is thornless and straight, O Varuṇa.
By that path, O Ādityas, speak for us and grant us protection that is difficult to overcome.
May Aditi, the daughter of royalty, and Aryaman carry us across all hostilities by easy ways.
May we, with many heroes, remain unharmed under the lofty protection of Mitra and Varuṇa.
They uphold the three earths and the three heavens; three are their ordinances within the assembly.
By the Eternal Law (ṛta), O Ādityas, your greatness is vast; that is beautiful, O Aryaman, Varuṇa, and Mitra.
They uphold the three celestial luminous realms; they are golden, pure, and purified by their own radiance.
Unborn from sleep, unblinking, undeceived, and far-famed, they exist for the sake of the upright mortal.
O Varuṇa, you are the king of all—both those who are gods, O Asura, and those who are mortals.
Grant us a hundred autumns to behold; may we attain the well-established lifespans of old.
O Ādityas, neither the right nor the left is distinguished by us, neither the east nor the west.
O Vasus, whether through simplicity or through wisdom, may we, led by you, attain the light that is free from fear.

He who offers gifts to the kings who abide by the cosmic order (*ṛta*), and whom the constant prosperities cause to grow—he goes forth as the first, wealthy man on his chariot, a giver of goods, praised in the assemblies.
Pure, undeceived, possessing excellent heroes, he dwells near waters that provide good pasture; he lives out his full span of life.

No one slays him from near or from afar who remains under the guidance of the Ādityas. O Aditi, Mitra, and Varuṇa, be gracious; whatever offense we have committed against you, forgive it. O Indra, grant us safety and light within Urvaśī; let not the long darknesses overtake us.

Both [worlds], meeting together, cause rain from heaven to swell for him; he, becoming fortunate, thrives in his renown. Conquering both dwellings, he goes forth to battles; both halves of the world become favorable to him.
O worshipful Ādityas, those wondrous powers of yours which are set out as snares for the enemy who seeks to harm.
Like a horse, may we pass over those who ride in their chariots; may we remain unharmed within your wide protection.
O Varuṇa, may I not experience the destitution of a dear, liberal, and helpful patron. O King, may I not be deprived of well-governed wealth. May we speak with great power...
May this [hymn] of the poet, the self-ruling Āditya, surpass all things in greatness.
I beg for the high renown of the abundant Varuṇa, the god who is delightful to worship. O Varuṇa, may we be fortunate under your ordinance, praising you with attentive minds.

May we, like fires that burn day after day, approach the dawns rich in cattle, O Varuṇa, our leader of wide renown; may we be under the protection of you, the possessor of many heroes. O undeceivable sons of Aditi, O gods, grant us your forgiveness for our kinship.
The Āditya, the Dispenser, has sent them forth; the rivers flow according to the *ṛta* of Varuṇa. They do not weary, nor do they cease; like birds, they fly swiftly across the expanse.
Loosen for us our sin like a tethering rope; O Varuṇa, may we succeed in your opening of the *ṛta*.

May the thread not break while I weave my prayer; may my measure not fail before the appointed time of the work. O Varuṇa, drive away fear from me; O sovereign Lord of Truth, hold me fast according to the Law.
Release me from sin as one releases a calf from its tether; for apart from you, not even for a moment’s blink do I have power.

O Varuṇa, do not strike us with those weapons of yours, O Asura, which consume the sinner who commits sin against you. May we not go forth from the light into exile; loosen our enemies completely so that we may live.
Homage to you, O Varuṇa, in the past, now, and even in the future—so shall we speak, O you of many births.
For in you, O hard-to-overcome one, rest your unshakable vows like mountains. Drive away the debts incurred by me; O King, let me not suffer for what another has done.
Many more dawns have yet to break; O Varuṇa, ordain that we may live through them.

O King, whoever—whether an ally or a friend—has spoken fear to me, who am afraid, in my dream; or whoever, like a thief or a wolf, seeks to harm us—O Varuṇa, protect us from that! May I not [be separated] from the liberal patrons...
O Ādityas, upholders of holy vows, vigorous ones, keep far from me the sin of those who act in secret, like a stingy miser.
O gods Varuṇa and Mitra, you who hear me, knowing the auspicious path, I call upon you for protection.
You, O gods, are our providence; you are our strength; you drive away our enemies to a distance.
O dispensers of gifts, be gracious and forgive us; show us mercy this day and in the future as well.
What indeed may we do for you with our future service, or what with our past friendship, O Vasus?
O Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Indra, and Maruts, grant us well-being.
O gods, you are indeed those who grant wealth; have mercy upon me, your suppliant. Let not your chariot be without a middle support, and let us not grow weary while seeking your protection.
I alone have fashioned many offerings for you, since you have instructed me like a father instructs a gambler.
Far away be the stones, far away the evils, O gods; do not seize me as one seizes a son.
O worshipful ones, turn toward us this day; trembling with fear, I would enter into your heart.
O gods, protect us from the devouring wolf; protect us, O worshipful ones, from the pit and from falling.
May I not [be separated from] the bounteous ones...
The waters do not rest for the god Savitṛ who performs the *ṛta*, nor for Indra the slayer of Ahi. Day after day the power of the waters passes away; how great was their first creation?
The Mother spoke forth to the wise one who was about to bring destruction upon Vṛtra.
Cutting paths for him according to his pleasure, the roaring rivers go day by day toward their goal.
For he has stood upright in the intermediate space; then he hurled his deadly weapon at Vṛtra.
Clothed in mist, he indeed surged forth from the waters; Indra, armed with sharp weapons, conquered the enemy.
O Bṛhaspati, pierce the heroes of the Asura Vṛkadvaras with your heat as if with fire.
Just as you have slain them even in former times with boldness, so now, O Indra, slay our enemy.
Cast down from on high the stone from heaven, with which, being exhilarated, you may utterly consume the enemy.
For the winning of offspring, of progeny, and of abundant wealth, O Indra, make us a sharer in the acquisition of cattle.
For you two indeed further the power of him whom you favor; you stand as the inciters of the worshipper who is diligent.
O Indra and Soma, protect us; in this time of fear, grant us a place of safety.
Let neither fatigue, nor weariness, nor sloth overcome me, nor let us say, "Do not press the Soma.
May he who gives to me, who bestows, who takes heed of me, and who comes with cattle to me as I press the Soma, [grant me his favor].
O Sarasvatī, aid us; accompanied by the Maruts, boldly conquer our enemies.
Indra slays that very one who is arrogant and displaying his strength, the bull of the Śaṇḍikas.
Whosoever seeks to harm us from afar or wishes to devour us—having seen him, pierce him with your sharpened weapon.
O Bṛhaspati, conquer the enemies with your weapons; O King, cast the malevolent one who seeks to harm us into confinement.

O Hero, perform those heroic deeds which are yours to accomplish, together with our own brave warriors. Let them remain long exposed to the smoke of your wrath; having slain them, bring back their riches to us.
Seeking your favor, I address with reverence that Marut host, the divine people,
so that we may obtain wealth consisting of all-heroic sons, along with progeny, renowned day by day.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, together with the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus, protect our chariot.
When they fly forth like birds from their dwelling, seeking glory, eager, and seated upon the trees;
then, O gods, being of one mind, protect our chariot that seeks booty among the people—
when the swift ones, crossing the mid-air with their strides, strike it down with their hooves upon the ridge of the earth.
And may that Indra, who belongs to all people, the one of excellent wisdom, come hither with the host of Maruts from heaven;
may he follow us with his wolf-averting aids for the sake of great gain and the winning of booty.
And may that god Tvaṣṭṛ, the overcomer of the world, in harmony with the goddesses, speed our chariot forward.

Iḷā, Bhaga, Bṛhaddiva, Rodasī, Pūṣan, Purandhi, and the Aśvins, the lords who bestow gifts; and those two goddesses, the auspicious ones of dual aspect, Dawn and Night, who incite all moving creatures—
since I praise you both, O Earth, with a new hymn, may you spread forth the threefold food for all that stands and moves.

And may Hiraṇyastūpa, Aja Ekapād, Trita, Ṛbhukṣan, and Savitṛ accept your praise like that of the Uśijs—Ahibudhnya and the Son of the Waters, who speeds with his swift steeds through our prayer and ritual labor.
These offerings I desire for you, O worshipful ones; the Āyus have fashioned them for you as something new.
Seeking renown and desiring booty, may we, like a chariot-horse, attain our prayer.
O Heaven and Earth, be the protectors of this my word, which I, a follower of *ṛta*, desire to accomplish.
For you two, whose wealth is most far-reaching, I, seeking riches, have here placed this great praise, O you who are celebrated from of old.
Let not secret harms from mortal man deceive us; do not deliver us over to these calamities.
Let our friendship not be severed; be mindful of this with a benevolent mind—for that very thing we pray to you.
With a gracious spirit, bring hither the willing cow, full of milk, overflowing, and inexhaustible.
With feet and with my voice, O much-invoked one, I urge you evermore—the swift, prize-winning steed.
I invoke Rākā, who is easily summoned, with a beautiful hymn; may the fortunate goddess hear us and take heed of us herself.
May she sew together our work with a needle that does not break, and may she grant us a son, a praiseworthy hero, who shall be worthy of the sacrificial bowl.
O Rākā, those well-formed favors of yours, with which you bestow riches upon the donor—
come to us today with those, benevolent and gracious, O fortunate one, granting thousandfold prosperity. O Sinīvālī, broad-tressed one, you who are the sister of the gods.
Enjoy the oblation offered; O Goddess, grant us progeny.
To her who has beautiful arms, beautiful fingers, who is prolific and brings forth many sons—to that Sinīvālī, the mistress of the people, offer the oblation.
She who is Guṅgū, she who is Sinīvālī, she who is Rākā, and she who is Sarasvatī—Indrāṇī I invoke for aid, and Varuṇānī for our well-being.
O Father of the Maruts, let your favor come to us; do not deprive us of the sight of the sun.
May the hero be gracious toward our horse; may we procreate offspring, O Rudra, through our progeny.
O Rudra, through these most healing medicines bestowed by you, may I attain a hundred winters. Drive far away from us hatred, drive away distress, and scatter the diseases in all directions.
O Rudra, you are the most excellent of all that is born in glory; you are the strongest of the strong, O wielder of the thunderbolt.
Carry us across to the further shore of distress with well-being; ward off all assaults of the malicious.
O Rudra, let us not provoke you to anger with our prostrations, nor with ill-praises, O Bull, nor with failed invocations.

Entrust our heroes to your healing remedies; I hear you are the best of physicians among physicians. I would propitiate Rudra with invocations, oblations, and hymns—he who is invoked with calls and offerings.
May he of the soft belly, the one easy to invoke, the tawny one with beautiful jaws, not deliver us over to this mental affliction.
The bull, accompanied by the Maruts, has gladdened me with his most vigorous strength as I implored him. Like one seeking shade from the heat, may I, O protector, enjoy the favor of Rudra.
Where, O Rudra, is that gracious hand of yours which possesses healing medicine and cooling power?
O Bearer-away of divine affliction, may you now indeed look with favor upon me, O Bull.
To the brown, white-shining Bull, I send forth a great and mighty hymn of praise. With prostrations we honor the radiant one; we celebrate the formidable name of Rudra.

With steady limbs, multiform, fierce, and tawny, you have adorned yourself with bright golden ornaments. From Rudra, the lord of this vast world, let not his asura-power depart. Worthy, you carry your arrows and your bow; worthy, you wear the worshipful, all-shaped golden breastplate.
O Worthy One, you take pity on this entire vast world; indeed, O Rudra, there is nothing more powerful than you.
Praise the famous one who sits upon the chariot-seat, the youthful, fierce, and terrible hunter like a wild beast.
O Rudra, being praised, be gracious to the singer; let your armies strike down someone other than us.
Even the youth bowed down before his father as he approached in homage; O Rudra, you praise the giver of abundance, the lord of the virtuous. Being praised, grant us healing remedies.
O Maruts, those pure remedies of yours, those most auspicious ones, O heroes, those that bring delight—[grant them to us].
Those boons which Manu chose for us, our father—those I desire as the health and well-being of Rudra.
May the missile of Rudra avoid us; may the great ill-will of the impetuous one pass us by.
O Bounteous One, relax your firm [bow] for the sake of the patrons; O Bestower of Boons, be gracious to our children and descendants.
Thus, O tawny bull, you who are observant, O God, so that you neither grow angry nor strike us down—be here, O Rudra, hearing our invocation; hear our great call!
The Maruts, pourers of rain, bold in their might, terrible like wild beasts, resplendent with their powers.
Like fires blazing, the Soma-pressers, blowing away the rushing wind, disclosed the cows.
Like the heavens with their stars, the armored ones shone forth; like rain from the clouds, they flashed with lightning.
O Maruts, with golden ornaments upon your breasts, when the fierce Rudra begot you in the bright udder of Pṛśni.
They sprinkle their horses like coursers in the race, hastening with the swift ears of the river.
O Maruts, wearing golden helmets and shaking them, you who are of one mind, come with your spotted deer for our nourishment.
They have grown strong for the sake of all beings, or rather, they are ever-givers of quickening gifts to Mitra.
With spotted horses, possessing inexhaustible wealth, they sit at the yoke like soaring birds in their appointed courses.
With blazing spears, along dustless paths, come with your kindling cows whose udders are full— O Maruts, of one mind, come like swans to their own resting places for the exhilaration of the mead.
O Maruts, of one mind, come to our prayers and to our libations like the praise of men;
swell the udder like a mare, and make the prayer beautiful with booty for the singer.
O Maruts, grant us that vigorous chariot, a drink that awakens the sacred word day by day.

Grant nourishment to the singers, to the poet in the assemblies, and the prize of wisdom— unharmed, invincible strength. When the Maruts, with golden ornaments upon their chests, yoke their horses to the chariots, O bounteous Bhaga,
like a cow swelling for her calf in the stalls, they pour forth great nourishment for the people who offer oblations.
O Maruts, O Vasus, whatever mortal enemy has set us at enmity, protect us from that injury!
Turn him back with your fiery wheel; O Rudras, strike down his weapon with your missile.
That wondrous course of yours, O Maruts, is made manifest when the sons of Pṛśni milked the udder of the cow, even though they were not her offspring.
Or when, O sons of Rudra, you irresistible ones, have drunk the soma pressed by Trita at the reproach of the singer who was wasting away;

those great Maruts, swift as birds, we invoke at the offering of the rushing Viṣṇu— those golden-hued, towering ones, with uplifted ladles, we, devoted to sacred prayer, seek for our praise-worthy bounty.
Those Daśagvas were the first to bring the sacrifice; may they incite us at the dawning of the mornings.
Like the Dawn, she uncovers the dark nights with her ruddy rays, shining with great light, a flood of cows.
Those Rudras have grown strong in the seats of Cosmic Order, together with the hosts and their ruddy ointments.
Gathering together with their swift power, they have assumed a most radiant and well-fashioned hue.
Coming as our great protection for our aid, we celebrate them with this homage,
just as Trita brought the five Hotṛ-priests hither for assistance, turning them downward for our protection.

That aid by which you carry the weak across distress, and by which you release the worshipper from reproach—may that favor of yours, O Maruts, come hither; may your benevolence approach us like a lowing cow.
Desiring strength, I have offered this eloquent speech; may the one who eats today accept my songs with pleasure.
Will the Son of the Waters, swift in his course, provide us with beautiful forms? For he shall surely take pleasure [in our offering].
From our own heart, we shall speak this mantra, well-fashioned; will he not indeed perceive it?
By the greatness of his divine power, the noble Son of the Waters has brought forth all beings.
Some come together, others approach; the rivers fill the common expanse.
Around him, the pure one, the radiant Son of the Waters, the pure waters have gathered.
Unto him, the youth, the smiling maidens—the waters—go forth, cleansing themselves.
He, bright and skillful, has shone forth with wealth for us—unfed by wood, clothed in ghee, within the waters.
For him, the three goddesses, unshakable women, offer food to the god.
For he has glided forward into the waters like one who has prepared them; he drinks the first-born milk of those who have borne before.
Here is the birthplace of the horse and of this [soma] that wards off the sky-enemy and the injurer; protect the patrons from harm.
Beyond the raw fortresses, the unassailable one—there the enemies shall perish, as shall all falsehoods.
In his own home is the cow easy to milk; she swells with the self-sustaining power (*svadhā*), and he, being strong, eats the food.
That Son of the Waters, bestowing strength within the waters, shines forth for the sake of the one who offers gifts to the worshiper.
He, the holy one, the observer of *ṛta*, who shines far and wide with pure divine splendor within the waters—
he is the one from whom all other worlds, like branches, and the plants are born through their progeny.
For the Son of the Waters has taken his station in the lap of the recumbent ones, standing erect and clothed in lightning.
Carrying his supreme majesty, the swift, golden-hued rivers flow around him.
He is of golden form, of golden appearance; that Son of the Waters is indeed of golden hue.
Seated from his golden womb, the giver of gold bestows food upon him.

That countenance of his, and his beloved name, the secret one, increases as the offspring of the waters. Him the young maidens kindle together thus; he is golden-hued, and clarified butter is his food.
To him, the lowest of many, our friend, let us do service with sacrifices, with homage, and with oblations.
I polish his back, I provide for him with hollowed logs, I nourish him with food, and I celebrate him all around with hymns.
He, the bull, begat the embryo within them; he, the infant, sucks them, and they lick him.
That Son of the Waters, of unblemished color, has here entered another body with his own form. Standing upon this highest step, shining forever without stains, the mighty waters,
bringing ghee as food for their offspring, fly around him with their own wings.
O Agni, I have offered a secure dwelling for the people; I have offered a well-fashioned hymn to the patrons.
All that...
For you, the Vasistha has urged on the cows and the waters; the men have milked them out with the pressing-stones.
Drink, O Indra, Svāhā! Drink the Soma offered with the *vaṣaṭ* call from the Hotṛ’s cup, for you are the first lord of it.
Blended with sacrifices, with spotted deer and spears, the radiant ones are dear in their ornaments as they go on their journey.
Sitting upon the sacrificial grass, O sons of Bharata, O heroes of heaven, drink the Soma from the Potṛ’s cup.

Come indeed to us, O you who are easily invoked; sit down upon the sacrificial grass and take your delight. Then, O Tvaṣṭṛ, being well-pleased with the soma juice, rejoice together with the gods and their wives in your excellent company.
O inspired sage, bring the gods here and perform the sacrifice; O Hotṛ, sit down in your three appointed places.
Accept the Soma-mead that has been set forth; drink from the Āgnīdhra vessel and satisfy yourself with your portion.
This [Soma] is for you, increasing the manly strength of your body; it has been placed in your arms as power from of old.
For you it is pressed, O Maghavan; for you it is brought. Drink of this, satisfied by the priestly formula (brāhmaṇa).

May you two enjoy the sacrifice; be mindful of my invocation. The Hotṛ priest has sat down according to the ancient invocations. O Kings, homage comes toward you both; come hither and drink the Soma-mead from the Praśāstṛ.
Rejoice at your pleasure in the Hotṛ’s portion of the plant; O Adhvaryus, he desires the full ladle poured out.
Therefore, bring this [oblation] for him; as one who grants wealth, drink the Soma from the *hotṛ*’s cup according to the seasons.
Him whom I previously invoked, him indeed I invoke now; he is the one to be invoked, the giver whose name is celebrated.
The Soma-mead set forth by the *adhvaryu*s—drink the Soma from the *potṛ*’s cup according to the seasons.
May thy draft-horses be fat, with which thou goest; O Lord of the Forest, be firm and unharmed.
Stretching forth, O bold one, having summoned [the gods], do thou bring the Soma from the office of the Neṣṭṛ.
He has drunk from the Hotṛ’s cup and from the Potṛ’s; he has exhilarated and has enjoyed the offered food from the Neṣṭṛ’s cup.
Let Draviṇodas drink from the fourth vessel—the uninjured, immortal cup—of him who bestows wealth.
Yoke today your hitherward-turning, swift chariot drawn by heroes; here is your place for unyoking.
Mix the oblations with honey; come quickly, O lords of ample wealth, and drink the Soma.
O Agni, accept the fuel; accept the oblation; accept the prayer of the people and accept the fair praise.
O Vasu, with all [the gods] and according to the season, being great and desiring them, cause the yearning gods to drink the oblation.
Up has risen that god Savitṛ for his impelling, the bearer of the sacrifice, for that most constant task.
Truly, he distributes treasure to the gods; then he grants a portion in well-being to the one who offers the oblation with a welcoming fire.
For the sake of all to hear him, the god stands upright; broad-handed, he stretches forth his arms.
Even the waters bend down at his command; even this wind rests as it wanders around.
Even those who travel with swift steeds he now surely causes to rest; even the weary man he has refreshed for this journey.
Even among the serpents he has brought them to rest; by Savitar’s decree, the release has come.
Weaving it out, she has spread it again; the wise one has placed his skill within the midst of his work.
Rising up, he has taken his stand; he has fixed the seasons apart. Savitṛ, the god, has come. The dwellings have various doors; Agni’s radiance spreads through all life, the source of light.
The Mother has bestowed the supreme portion upon her son; she has followed his banner, impelled by Savitṛ.
He who was established there, seeking victory, has returned; the desire of all who wander has been fulfilled.
Having left behind the waters and his altered form, he has gone according to the ordinance of the divine Savitṛ.
By you, O Apām Napāt, the portion placed within the waters has been secured; the thirsty ones have spread out across the desert wastes.
The forests do not violate those laws of this god Savitar; no one among the birds can transgress them.

As Varuṇa makes his dwelling-place ready for attainment, he, flickering with restless speed, watches even as he blinks. Every bird of the egg has entered its nest like a beast into its pen; Savitar has distributed all living beings according to their stations.
RV_02.038.09.1 His law neither Indra, nor Varuṇa, nor Mitra, nor Aryaman, nor Rudra violates;
nor do the enemies. Him, this god Savitṛ, I invoke for well-being with prostrations.
RV_02.038.10.1 May Bhaga, Dhiya, Vāja, Purandhi, Narāśaṃsa, and Gnāspati protect us as we strive for strength.
May we be dear to the god Savitṛ in the gathering of his lovely wealth.
From you, O Heaven, Waters, and Earth, may that desirable gift which you have bestowed come to us—
that which shall be a blessing to the praisers, to our kinsman, and to the singer who extols you widely, O Savitṛ.
Like two pressing-stones, you two sing this very praise here; like two vultures toward a tree containing a treasure;
like two priests at the assembly, chanting hymns; like two messengers of the people, you carry oblations to many places.
Setting out early in the morning like two chariot-heroes, like two kings, O Aśvins, you follow the chosen path together.
Like two women adorning their bodies, like a husband and wife who find wisdom among the people;
Like two horns, come first toward us; like two hooves, moving swiftly with your steeds.
Like two *cakravāka* birds at daybreak, come hither at dawn; O powerful ones, come like two chariot-drivers.
Like two ships, carry us across; like two yokes, like two hubs, like two inner wheels, like two outer wheels.
Like two dogs that do not harm our bodies, like two crabs, protect us from falling apart.
Like two winds that do not age, like the flow of rivers, like two eyes with their sight, come hither!
Like two hands most beneficial to the body, like two feet, lead us toward greater prosperity.
Like two lips speaking honeyed words, like two breasts, nourish us with the breath of life.
Like two nostrils, be the protectors of our bodies; like two ears, be well-hearing for us.
Like two hands, bestow power upon us; like two feet, traverse for us the realms of space.
O Aśvins, sharpen these songs of ours, which are devoted to you, as one sharpens an axe with a whetstone.
O Aśvins, the Gṛtsamadas have fashioned these prayers and hymns of praise as strengthening offerings for you.
O heroes, come hither, graciously accepting those [offerings]...
O Soma and Pūṣan, you two are the progenitors of riches, the progenitors of heaven, the progenitors of earth;
born as the guardians of the entire world, the gods have made you the navel of immortality.
May these two gods, at their birth, be pleased; may they hide away the unwanted darkness.
Within the raw cows, Indra brought forth the cooked [milk] for Soma and Pūṣan.
O Soma and Pūṣan, [you mounted] the seven-wheeled chariot that measures the mid-region and moves everywhere.
Him who is harnessed by the mind, moving in all directions, that five-reined steed—O Bulls, quicken him! One has made his seat high in heaven; the other is upon the earth and in the mid-air.
May those two release for us an increase of wealth, rich in many boons and rich in food, as a central point for us.
One has generated all beings; the other moves along, beholding the universe.
O Soma and Pūṣan, protect my prayer; with you two may we conquer all hostile armies.
May Pūṣan, the inspirer of all, quicken our prayer; may Soma, the lord of wealth, bestow riches upon us.
May the goddess Aditi, who is free from enemies, protect us.
... O Vāyu, with those thousandfold chariots that are yours, come hither; drawn by your teams of horses, come for the drinking of the Soma.
O Vāyu, accompanied by your team of horses, come! This bright [soma] is offered to you.
You shall go to the house of the one who presses the juice.
Today, O Indra and Vāyu, [partake] of the bright [soma] mixed with milk, you who possess the teams of horses.
Come hither, O heroes, and drink!
O Mitra and Varuṇa, increasers of Truth, this Soma has been pressed for you; hear my invocation here.
The two kings, free from malice, sit upon the firm, highest seat;
they dwell upon a thousand-pillared foundation.
They are the sovereign rulers, drinkers of clarified butter, the Ādityas, lords of the gift.
If you two are mindful of that which is not to be disregarded—
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, Rudras, lords of men— come hither with cattle and horses to our dwelling that protects us.
O Lords of ample wealth, let no enemy from afar nor any from near prevail against us,
nor any mortal foe who speaks evil. O Aśvins, bring to us that wealth which is radiant in appearance.
The two who occupy the sacrificial seats, the finders of wide space.
Indra indeed shall drive away even great fear; for he, the far-seeing one, is steadfast.
May Indra be gracious to us; may no evil reach us from behind. May there be good fortune for us from the front.
May Indra grant us freedom from fear from all directions.
The conqueror of enemies, all-seeing.
O All-Gods, come hither; hear this my invocation;
sit down upon this sacred grass.
This intense, honey-sweet, exhilarating draught is for you among the Śunahotras;
drink this which is desired.
O you who have Indra as your chief...
O Sarasvatī, most expansive, most flowing, most divine!
We are as if unworthy of praise; O Mother, grant us renown.
In you, O goddess Sarasvatī, all lifespans are centered.
Rejoice in the offerings of Śunahotra; O Goddess, grant us offspring. O Sarasvatī, rich in prizes, accept these prayers.
O upholder of Truth, those cherished thoughts of Gṛtsamada which they offer to you among the gods—accept them.
We choose you two today, the deceased ones who bring prosperity to the sacrifice,
and Agni, the bearer of oblations.
May Heaven and Earth make this our offering successful today, reaching unto the sky.
May they bestow sacrifice upon the gods. May the gods worthy of sacrifice sit upon your non-deceptive lap here today for the drinking of Soma.
Crying out repeatedly, proclaiming his birth, he sends forth his voice like a rower propelling a boat.
O auspicious bird, be a bringer of good fortune; let no calamity from any quarter find you.
Let not the hawk strike you down, nor the falcon; let not the archer with his arrow find you.
Crying out toward the direction of the fathers, may you, auspicious and a speaker of blessings, speak here.
Cry down from the right side of our houses, O bird, auspicious and a speaker of blessings. Let not the thief nor the malevolent one have power over us; [may there be] great...
The poets sing around thee in circumambulation, like birds that speak at the proper season.
Like a singer of the *Sāman*, thou utterest both voices; thou shinest forth according to the *Gāyatrī* and the *Triṣṭubh* meters.
O bird, like a *Udgātṛ* priest, thou singest the *Sāman*; like a son of the *Brahman*, thou recitest at the libations.
Like a vigorous stallion approaching mares, O Śakuna, proclaim auspiciousness to us from every side; O Śakuna, proclaim merit to us from all sides.
Speaking aloud, O Śakuna, proclaim auspiciousness to us; sitting silently, consider our well-being. When you fly up and cry out like a *karkari* bird, let it be with a great voice.
